result.title: A System 1 Decision Model for Medical Multiple-Choice Questions Built on Frozen Language Models
result.summary: A System 1 model answers a multiple-choice question in a single pass. A frozen language model turns the question and each option into vectors, two small, trained heads place them in a shared space, and the closest option wins. The design has been shown on agent decisions, but we are not aware of a study of how far it goes on exam questions that need medical knowledge, where the right option is often no more similar to the question than the wrong ones. We rebuilt the recipe from scratch for MedMCQA and trained only two projection heads and one temperature on top of frozen Qwen3.5-0.8B, Granite-4.2-3B and Qwen3-8B, using a contrastive loss with in-batch and hard negatives and a mask for repeated answers. With plain last-token vectors, both small encoders answer about one question in three correctly (33.1% and 33.0% on 3,842 held-out questions, where chance is 25.0%). Writing each text inside a one-word-summary prompt and lowering the learning rate of the heads raised this to 41.7% and 42.5% for the two small encoders and to 46.0% +-0.2 (three seeds) for Qwen3-8B. Shuffling the questions against the options returns accuracy to chance, so the heads do use the question. Flan-PaLM and Med-PaLM 2 report 57.6% and 72.3% on MedMCQA under a different protocol, so ours is a cheap, fast baseline and not a competitive system. We also say what our evidence cannot show: validation gains were about 1.7 to 2 times the test gains, and we could not separate the effect of reading several encoder layers from the other changes.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在冻结语言模型之上只训练两个投影头和一个温度，用含 in-batch 与 hard negative 的对比损失把 MedMCQA 的题干与选项映射到共享空间，以最近选项单次作答，并报告小模型约 33%、改进后 42%–46% 的准确率及打乱题干即回落随机的对照。
AI.relevance_reason: 「冻结表示 + 轻量相似度读出」可供核查作为判断内部状态是否保留任务必要信息的探针，其单向量相似度判别力有限的负结果也可能旁证池化导致的信息坍缩；但论文无视觉输入、无推理期状态更新，联系较远。
